Subject: Committed multi-region Dedicated: pricing & DR options

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the call yesterday. We're ready to talk numbers for a committed Dedicated deployment that is geo-distributed. High-level requirements:
- Primary region: us-west, steady baseline ~32 A100-equivalent GPUs for production traffic.
- Secondary region (DR / failover): eu-west, standby ~8 GPUs.
- Expected monthly token volume: ~5B tokens (mostly generation).
- Latency SLO: P95 < 120ms for typical production prompts; availability target 99.9%.
- Need options for automated cross-region routing and a DR failover exercise twice per year.

Questions for Redwood:
1) How do you price committed capacity across regions? Do you recommend separate per-region reserved pools or a single global commit that we can anchor to regions?
2) What does replication / standby pricing look like (hot standbys vs. cold)?
3) Do you offer credits for DR testing or failover windows?
4) What discount tiers should we expect for 12- and 24-month commits, and are multi-region deals eligible for extra volume discounts?
5) Any constraints on throughput guarantees across regions and how those are measured?

Can you send an example pricing worksheet and a short explainer of packaging options? We'll loop in procurement after we get initial numbers.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Finovate

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@finovate.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Committed multi-region Dedicated: pricing & DR options

Elena—

Appreciate the clear requirements. I've attached a short pricing workbook (Committed_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx) and outline below two pragmatic ways customers typically structure multi-region Dedicated commitments. I'll also summarize numbers so procurement has something to work with right away.

Option A — Per-region reserved pools (recommended when data residency or isolated telemetry is needed):
- You reserve 32 GPUs in us-west and 8 GPUs in eu-west as two separate dedicated pools.
- Discounts: 12-month commit = ~15% off list, 24-month = ~25% off list.
- Replication/standby: priced as an add-on. Hot-standby (synchronous KV replication + warm compute) typically 18%–22% of the active pool monthly commit per standby region depending on the level of readiness. Cold standby (image + pre-warming) is a smaller fixed fee.
- Failover testing: we can provide 2 DR tests per year with no charge; additional tests billed at a reduced hourly ops rate or consumed from a small testing credit allowance.
- Throughput guarantees: we size per GPU for expected QPS/throughput (we'll include modeled throughput in the workbook). SLOs backed by the Dedicated SLA; additional SLO guarantees (lower latency percentiles) are possible with higher commit or dedicated isolation.

Option B — Global-commit (geo-anchor) with regional anchors (recommended when you want flexible cross-region routing and blended pricing):
- You commit to a global pool equivalent (40 GPUs total) but create regional anchors (32 in us-west, 8 in eu-west) in our control plane for routing & telemetry.
- Discounting is blended, and we can offer an additional 3%–5% consolidation discount compared to per-region commits for the same committed GPU count.
- Replication: active-active replication option available; replication premium for active-active is higher (25%–30% of equivalent active pool cost) because it requires steering, real-time KV sync, and additional network egress and capacity.
- Failover testing: included twice annually plus a small credits bucket for runbook rehearsals.

Preliminary commercial numbers (ballpark):
- Baseline list: $7,500 / GPU / month (A100-equivalent) — used as list for modeling only.
- Option A monthly (list): us-west (32 GPUs) = $240k; eu-west (8 GPUs) = $60k; total list = $300k/mo. With a 12-month 15% commit discount -> ~$255k/mo.
- Replication (hot standby) for eu-west at 20% of active pool = ~$12k/mo additional.
- Option B blended discount example (24-month): list $300k -> 25% discount = $225k/mo and consolidation discount say additional 4% -> ~$216k/mo; active-active replication add-on would be ~25% on top if requested.

Notes and tradeoffs:
- Per-region commits make accounting and cost allocation straightforward for procurement.
- Global-commit gives you flexibility to shift capacity and often nets a slightly better blended unit cost.
- Replication pricing is the main variable — we can structure it as % of active committed pool or a fixed per-GPU standby fee (finance prefers the latter for predictability).

Next steps:
- I recommend we present the two options to procurement with the attached workbook showing line-item math and three pricing scenarios (12m, 24m, active-active).
- If you like, we can schedule a short call next week to walk through the workbook.

I'll loop in our pricing manager and legal for any SLA exception asks once you indicate a preferred path.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Committed_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx (pricing workbook, three scenarios)

Diego —

Quick thoughts from finance/product perspective:
- Discounting: avoid >25% off list on GPU commits unless there's a strong multi-year lock and clear expansion commitments. Our floor for 24-months with that scale should be around 22% unless we get an up-front payment or expansion cadence.
- Replication pricing: I prefer a predictable per-GPU standby fee (e.g., 20% of active as a default, but expressed as a fixed $/GPU to procurement). That makes chargebacks easier for customers. For this account, 18% is OK only if they commit to 24 months and auto-expand by +10% if usage grows.
- DR tests: two complimentary run-throughs per year is reasonable, anything beyond should come from a testing credit line we include in the deal. Do not make SLA credits contingent on unlimited tests.
- Throughput/latency SLOs: confirm with product on how we measure regional traffic when cross-region routing is enabled — e.g., routing adds network tail latency we shouldn't guarantee unless routed through a particular region.

I'll carve out time next week to look at the workbook. If Diego wants to offer a 3% consolidation credit for the global-commit option, we need to bake that into the margin model.

-Aditya
VP, Pricing & Revenue Ops
